q: Explain the difference between Recioto and Amarone in one line.
accept: recioto sweet fermentation stopped amarone fermented dry
ans: Same appassimento fruit; Recioto's fermentation is arrested sweet, Amarone's runs dry
exp: Amarone means 'the bitter one' — named against Recioto's sweetness.

q: Canadian VQA Icewine requires the grapes to be pressed at what minimum cold and what minimum must weight?
exp: Canada's standard is the strictest icewine law in the world and is enforced: grapes must freeze naturally on the vine, be picked and pressed while frozen at -8°C or below, and reach 35 °Brix, with artificial freezing — cryoextraction — expressly prohibited. Germany's Eiswein is the near-miss distractor at -7°C with a must weight in the Beerenauslese band, and unlike botrytised wines both laws want clean, unrotted fruit. The cold does the concentration by leaving water behind as ice in the press.

q: Since the 2013 reform, what is the legal minimum residual sugar for Tokaji Aszú, and what became of the lower puttonyos?
accept: 120 grams per litre minimum with three and four puttonyos abolished
minimum 120 g/l residual sugar and puttonyos now optional
only five and six puttonyos remain the minimum is 120 g/l
aszu must reach 120 g/l and age eighteen months in wood
ans: 120 g/L residual sugar — the old 5 puttonyos level. The 3 and 4 puttonyos categories were abolished, and the puttonyos number is now optional on the label, permitted only as 5 or 6. Aszú must also spend at least 18 months in wood
exp: Hungary raised the floor deliberately: the weaker Aszú tiers were undercutting the name, so the category now starts where 5 puttonyos used to. This is a case where the law has moved well ahead of the textbooks — a candidate who describes 3 puttonyos Aszú as a current category is quoting a rulebook that was withdrawn. Note also that the puttony itself, the 25 kg hod of aszú berries, is now a historical measure rather than a legal one.

q: How is Pedro Ximénez prepared for sweet Sherry, and what residual sugar minimum does the DO set for it?
accept: asoleo sun drying on esparto mats with a 212 g/l minimum
sun dried on mats then fortified minimum 212 grams residual sugar
raisined in the sun and mutaged 212 g/l for px
asoleo then fortification px 212 g/l moscatel 160
ans: Asoleo — the picked grapes are sun-dried on esparto grass mats for roughly one to two weeks until raisined — then pressed with difficulty and fortified almost at once; DO Jerez requires a minimum 212 g/L residual sugar for Pedro Ximénez (160 g/L for Moscatel)
exp: PX is the extreme of the raisining family — finished wines routinely carry 400–500 g/L, far above the legal floor — and its blackness comes from the sun and from long oxidative solera ageing, not from any red grape. Note the division of labour: much PX fruit is grown in Montilla-Moriles, where the variety ripens more reliably, and moved to Jerez. Distinguish these naturally sweet wines from Cream, which is a dry base sweetened after the fact.

q: Define 'diurnal range' and name a region that weaponizes it.
accept: difference between day and night temps
ans: The day–night temperature swing; e.g., Uco Valley, Cafayate, Columbia Valley — sugar by day, acid preserved by night

q: Which climate classification system counts growing-degree days into Regions I–V?
ans: The Winkler Index (Amerine & Winkler, UC Davis)
exp: Region I: Champagne-cool; Region V: Fresno-hot. Huglin's index is the European rival.

q: Albariza's agronomic gift to Jerez is:
ans: Storing winter rain deep beneath a baked summer crust — vines drink through the drought
exp: Diatomaceous chalk; the whitest soils grow the finest Palomino.

q: Galestro and alberese are the paired soils of:
ans: Chianti Classico (galestro: friable schist-clay; alberese: hard limestone)

q: Why do slopes beat flats for frost?
ans: Cold air flows downhill past the vines (katabatic drainage) — frost pools on valley floors
exp: Hence mid-slope 'thermal belts' hold the classic crus.
Free marks at Advanced — say the rock, the place, and the mechanism.

accept: mountains force air to rise and drop moisture
orographic lift wrings out storms leeward dry
ans: Mountains force moist air up (orographic lift), wringing out rain; the lee side stays dry
exp: Cascades/Columbia, Vosges/Alsace, Andes/Mendoza — the exam's three.

q: Limestone's celebrated vineyard property, beyond drainage, is:
accept: holds moisture while draining high ph
ans: Its capillarity — draining excess yet holding reserve moisture, plus high-pH effects on vine chemistry
exp: Whether you can taste it remains chemistry's favorite bar fight.

q: 'Ungrafted' survives naturally in which three soil/geography refuges?
accept: sandy soils volcanic ash geographic isolation
ans: Deep sands (Colares, Lodi), volcanic ash (Santorini, Etna pockets), and isolated/quarantined lands (Chile, South Australia)
exp: Phylloxera cannot tunnel or hold galleries in loose sand or ash; isolation and quarantine keep it out of Chile and South Australia altogether.

q: The Humboldt and Benguela currents matter to wine because they:
accept: chill fog onto chile and south africa coasts
ans: Chill coastal air (Chile; South Africa), sending fog and cool wind into vineyards at low latitudes
exp: Cold water lets the 30s-latitudes grow Pinot and Sauvignon.

q: Basalt-derived soils tend to confer which traits, per Etna and Willamette partisans?
accept: iron rich water retentive dark soils
ans: Iron-rich darkness, good water retention, and (advocates claim) smoky, ferrous savor with acid freshness
exp: Say the observable: the wines run fresher than their latitude suggests.

accept: field selection from many vines vs single clone
massale cuttings from diverse old vines
ans: Massal: propagating cuttings from many diverse estate vines; clonal: multiplying one certified clone
exp: Diversity vs predictability — old-vine estates guard their massal heritage.
